Geographic focus:

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references 2024 baseline, YTD 2026 issuance data, recent deal activity
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — permitting delays, grid connection freezes, weakening debt demand signals
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — $3T data center spending through 2028, concentration risk for insurers, structural credit tightening

Synopsis:
AI-related debt issuance has exploded to ~$500B YTD in 2026 (~20% of all high-grade US issuance vs. 1% in 2024), but the easy money phase is over. Lenders are repricing risk upward and imposing structural protections — milestone-gated drawdowns, long-term tenant backstops (Meta, Nvidia), and asset pledges. Even investment-grade hyperscaler bonds (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle) now trade at a premium to peers, with oversubscription ratios collapsing from ~5x to <2x. Key forward risks center on delivery bottlenecks (chips, permits, grid access), not demand, with Texas grid delays alone threatening ~50GW of pipeline. Riskier credits like CoreWeave face double-digit yields despite collateral. Structural credit deterioration in AI infrastructure financing is now clearly in motion.
